To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new method for the characterization of colloidal aggregates from static images.
we developed two novel cluster analysis summary functions for the study of colloidal aggregates, which are related to graph theory.
we show how to study DLCA and RLCA from experimental data and how to use the obtained results to characterize a colloidal system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a quantitative link between static micrographs and particle aggregation dynamics in colloidal gels.
a quantitative link between static images of colloidal structures and aggregation dynamics, which is a prerequisite for the development of models for the dynamics of colloidal aggregation.
the quantitative comparison of experimental data with simulations of cluster aggregation models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DLCA process is not the correct model for the studied colloidal system.
the RLCA model fits the experimental data slightly better than the DLAC model, but that both models can describe the data.
the RLCA model describes the experimental data well and that DLCA does not describe the data at all.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the probability of aggregation can be quantified from static micrographs, allowing for a comparison with cluster aggregation models and thus for a better understanding of colloidal aggregation.
we show how to use summary functions to study particle aggregates in three dimensions.
the probability of aggregation can be quantified from static images and that this information allows for a comparison of experimental data and simulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probability of aggregation can be quantitatively evaluated from static micrographs.
it is possible to study aggregation processes from static micrographs and to compare the results to simulation data.
it is possible to use static micrographs to study aggregation dynamics in three‐dimensional colloidal systems.
